concepts.name: Translating age statements
concepts.description: Turning 'years ago' and 'years hence' into algebra.

concepts.name: Constant difference
concepts.description: The gap between two people's ages never changes.

concepts.name: Age ratios over time
concepts.description: Ratios of ages change even though differences do not.

concepts.name: Family and group ages
concepts.description: Sums, averages and multi-person age problems.

formulas.title: Past and future ages
formulas.prompt: If someone is x years old now, how do you write their age n years ago and n years from now?
formulas.formula:
n years ago: x − n
n years hence: x + n
formulas.explanation: Always anchor the unknown at the present age. Every other time in the question is then a shift from it.
formulas.example:
A is 25 now
5 years ago: 20
5 years hence: 30
formulas.commonMistake: Setting the unknown at a past age, which makes every other statement harder to write.
formulas.applicationPrompt: A is x years old today. How do you write his age 5 years ago?

formulas.title: The difference never changes
formulas.prompt: What stays constant between two people's ages?
formulas.formula: Age difference is the same at every point in time
formulas.explanation: Both people age at the same rate, so the gap is fixed forever. Ratios, however, change constantly.
formulas.example:
Father 40, son 12 → gap 28
In 5 years: 45 and 17 → still 28
formulas.commonMistake: Assuming a ratio stays fixed over time the way a difference does.
formulas.applicationPrompt: A father is 40 and his son 12. What will their age difference be in 5 years?

formulas.title: Setting up an age ratio
formulas.prompt: Two present ages are in the ratio a : b. How do you write them?
formulas.formula: Present ages = ax and bx, then apply the time shift to both

variables.meaning: the common multiplier to solve for

formulas.explanation: Writing both ages with a single unknown keeps the problem to one equation.
formulas.example:
Ratio 4 : 3 now, 6 : 5 in 6 years
(4x + 6)/(3x + 6) = 6/5 → x = 3
Ages: 12 and 9
formulas.commonMistake: Adding the years to only one of the two ages.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Two ages are in the ratio 4 : 3 today. How do you represent them?

formulas.title: Sum of ages over time
formulas.prompt: How does the sum of several people's ages change over n years?
formulas.formula: New sum = Old sum + (number of people × n)
formulas.explanation: Everyone ages by n, so a group of k people adds kn years in total.
formulas.example:
Three people total 60 now
In 5 years: 60 + 3 × 5 = 75
formulas.commonMistake: Adding n only once rather than once per person.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Three people's ages total 60. What will the total be in 5 years?

formulas.title: Make the gap in both ratios equal
formulas.prompt: The ratio of two ages is given now and again some years later. How do you avoid algebra?
formulas.formula:
Scale the ratios until both have the same difference.
One part = years passed ÷ change in either term
formulas.explanation: The real age gap never changes, so the two ratios must show the same number of parts between the ages.
formulas.example: Now 3 : 5, in 6 years 2 : 3. Rewrite 2 : 3 as 4 : 6 (gap 2, like 3 : 5). Each term rose by 1 part = 6 years, so the ages are 18 and 30.
formulas.commonMistake: Comparing 3 : 5 with 2 : 3 directly, although their parts are different sizes.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Ages are in the ratio 4 : 7 now and will be 5 : 8 in 5 years.

levels.title: Turning Sentences into Equations
levels.description: Age problems are translation exercises. Get the translation right and the algebra is easy.

blocks.title: Anchor at the present
blocks.body:
Let the unknown be a present age. Then '5 years ago' is x − 5 and 'in 5 years' is x + 5. If you anchor at a past age instead, every other statement needs extra care.

Write the present ages first, then shift them.
The age difference between two people is fixed for life. A ratio is not. If a question gives a ratio at two different times, the difference is the quantity you can trust.

blocks.title: A worked translation
blocks.body:
"A father is three times as old as his son. In 10 years he will be twice as old."

Son now = x, father now = 3x
In 10 years: 3x + 10 = 2(x + 10)
3x + 10 = 2x + 20 → x = 10

Son is 10, father is 30. Check: in 10 years, 40 is twice 20 ✓

blocks.title: Always check your answer
blocks.body: Age problems are self-checking: substitute your answer back into the original sentence. It takes ten seconds and catches nearly every translation slip.

levels.title: Age Relationships
levels.description: The four relationships behind every age question.

levels.title: Ratios Across Time
levels.description: Two-time-point problems solved with a single unknown.

questions.question: A is 25 years old today. How old was she 8 years ago?

hints.text: Going back in time means subtracting.

questions.question: A father is 40 and his son is 12. What will the difference between their ages be in 5 years?
questions.explanation: Both age by 5 years, so the difference stays 28 — as it always will.

hints.text: Both people age at exactly the same rate.

questions.question: The ages of three friends add up to 60 years today. What will their total age be in 5 years?
questions.explanation: Each of the three gains 5 years, so the total rises by 15 to 75.
solutionSteps: Three people gain 3 × 5 = 15 years in total.

hints.text: How many people are ageing?
Each adds 5 years to the total.

commonMistakes: Adding only 5 years to the total.

questions.question: The present ages of two people are in the ratio 3 : 4. What is the best way to represent them?
questions.explanation: Writing them as 3x and 4x builds the ratio in and leaves just one unknown to solve for.
solutionSteps: A ratio fixes the proportion but not the size.
3x and 4x are in the ratio 3 : 4 for any x.
One unknown means one equation is enough.

hints.text: You need a representation that works for any actual pair of ages.

commonMistakes: Treating the ratio numbers as the actual ages.

questions.question: The ratio between two people's ages stays the same as the years pass.
questions.explanation: A 10-year-old and a 20-year-old are in the ratio 1 : 2, but ten years later they are 20 and 30 — a ratio of 2 : 3. Only the difference is constant.
solutionSteps: Take ages 10 and 20, a ratio of 1 : 2.
After 10 years: 20 and 30, a ratio of 2 : 3.
The ratio changed, so the statement is false.

hints.text: Try a simple pair of ages and move forward ten years.
Ratios drift towards 1 : 1 as people get older.

commonMistakes: Confusing the constant difference with a constant ratio.

questions.question: The present ages of A and B are in the ratio 4 : 3. In 6 years the ratio will be 6 : 5. What is A's present age?
questions.explanation: With ages 4x and 3x, (4x + 6)/(3x + 6) = 6/5 gives 20x + 30 = 18x + 36, so x = 3 and A is 12.

hints.text: Write both ages using a single unknown x.
Add 6 to BOTH ages before forming the new ratio.
Cross multiply (4x + 6) × 5 = (3x + 6) × 6.

questions.question: A father is three times as old as his son. In 10 years he will be twice as old as his son. How old is the son now?
questions.explanation: With son = x and father = 3x, 3x + 10 = 2(x + 10) gives x = 10.
solutionSteps: Check: father 30, son 10; in 10 years 40 and 20 ✓
questions.method: Translate both time points, then solve.

hints.text: Call the son's present age x and write the father's in terms of it.
Add 10 to both ages for the future statement.

questions.question: A is twice as old as B today. Five years ago, A was three times as old as B. How old is B now?
questions.explanation: With B = x and A = 2x, 2x − 5 = 3(x − 5) gives x = 10.
solutionSteps: Let B = x now, so A = 2x.
Check: A was 15 and B was 5 five years ago ✓
questions.method: Subtract 5 from both ages for the past statement.

hints.text: Let B's present age be x.
Five years ago both were 5 years younger.

questions.question: A is 6 years older than B. In 4 years' time, the sum of their ages will be 50 years. How old is A now? (Answer in years)
questions.explanation: In 4 years both are 4 years older, so their present ages add up to 50 − 8 = 42. A is 6 years older than B, so A = (42 + 6) ÷ 2 = 24 and B = 18. Check: in 4 years they will be 28 and 22, which add up to 50.
solutionSteps: In 4 years the sum grows by 2 × 4 = 8.
questions.method: Sum and difference: the larger age = (sum + difference) ÷ 2.

hints.text: Bring the future sum back to the present: each person loses 4 years.
Now you know the sum and the difference of the present ages.
Larger = (sum + difference) ÷ 2.

commonMistakes: Subtracting only 4 from the sum instead of 8 (getting 26).
Giving B's age (18) instead of A's.

questions.question: The sum of the ages of a father and son is 45 years. Five years ago, the father was six times as old as his son. How old is the son now?
questions.explanation: With son = s and father = 45 − s, (45 − s − 5) = 6(s − 5) gives 40 − s = 6s − 30, so s = 10.
solutionSteps: Check: father 35, son 10; five years ago 30 = 6 × 5 ✓
questions.method: Use the sum to express both ages with one unknown.

hints.text: The sum lets you write the father's age as 45 − s.
Subtract 5 from both ages for the past statement.

commonMistakes: Applying the 'six times' condition to present ages.

questions.question: The average age of a family of 4 is 28 years. A baby aged 3 joins the family. What is the new average age? (Answer in years)
questions.explanation: Total = 112; adding the baby gives 115 across 5 people, so the average is 23.
solutionSteps: After the baby joins: 112 + 3 = 115, across 5 people.
questions.method: Convert averages to totals before changing the group.

hints.text: Find the family's total age first.
Remember the count rises to 5.

questions.question: The present ages of A and B are in the ratio 3 : 5. Four years ago, their ages were in the ratio 1 : 2. What will be the ratio of A's age to B's age 8 years from now?
questions.explanation: Let the present ages be 3x and 5x. Four years ago: (3x − 4) : (5x − 4) = 1 : 2, so 6x − 8 = 5x − 4 and x = 4. The ages are 12 and 20. In 8 years they will be 20 and 28, and 20 : 28 = 5 : 7.
questions.method: Find the actual ages from the two ratios, then move them to the asked time.

hints.text: Write the present ages as 3x and 5x.
Subtract 4 from both and set the ratio equal to 1 : 2.
Add 8 to both actual ages before forming the new ratio.

questions.question: The present ages of A, B and C add up to 90 years. Six years ago, their ages were in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3. What is C's present age? (Answer in years)
questions.explanation: Six years ago each of the three was 6 years younger, so their ages then added up to 90 − 3 × 6 = 72. Split 72 in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3: the ages were 12, 24 and 36. Add 6 to each: today they are 18, 30 and 42. C is 42.
solutionSteps: Six years ago the total was 90 − 3 × 6 = 72.
questions.method: Move the total to the time of the ratio, split it, then move each age back.

hints.text: What was the total of the three ages six years ago?
Split that old total in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3.
Add 6 years back to C's old age.

commonMistakes: Subtracting only 6, not 18, from the total.
